questions.q: Determine whether the points $A(-2,1)$, $B(2,4)$, $C(5,0)$ form a right triangle, using the squared side lengths.
questions.answer: $AB^2=4^2+3^2=25$. $BC^2=3^2+4^2=25$. $AC^2=7^2+1^2=50$. Since $AB^2+BC^2=50=AC^2$, the triangle has a right angle at $B$.

questions.q: Determine whether the triangle with vertices $A(1,2)$, $B(5,2)$, $C(3,6)$ is isosceles.
questions.answer: $AC=\sqrt{2^2+4^2}=\sqrt{20}$ and $BC=\sqrt{2^2+4^2}=\sqrt{20}$, so $AC=BC$ and the triangle is isosceles.

sections.heading: The perpendicular bisector of a segment

questions.q: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $(2,3)$ and $(8,7)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint $=(5,5)$. Segment gradient $=\dfrac{7-3}{8-2}=\dfrac{2}{3}$, so the perpendicular gradient is $-\dfrac{3}{2}$. Equation: $y-5=-\dfrac{3}{2}(x-5)\Rightarrow y=-\dfrac{3}{2}x+\dfrac{25}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $(0,0)$ and $(6,8)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint $=(3,4)$. Segment gradient $=\dfrac{8}{6}=\dfrac{4}{3}$, so the perpendicular gradient is $-\dfrac{3}{4}$. Equation: $y-4=-\dfrac{3}{4}(x-3)\Rightarrow y=-\dfrac{3}{4}x+\dfrac{25}{4}$.

questions.q: A line segment has endpoints $(1,5)$ and $(7,5)$. Find the equation of its perpendicular bisector.
questions.answer: Midpoint $=(4,5)$. The segment is horizontal (gradient $0$), so the perpendicular bisector is the vertical line $x=4$.

answers: Distance from center $=\sqrt{(14-5)^2+(9-5)^2}=\sqrt{81+16}=\sqrt{97}\approx9.85$ meters, which is less than the radius $12$, so the tree lies inside the watered region.
